items.stem: What is the correct order of the four steps in one atomic layer deposition (ALD) cycle?
choices: Precursor pulse -> reactant pulse -> purge -> pump-out
Precursor pulse -> purge -> reactant pulse -> purge
Simultaneous precursor and reactant injection -> purge -> plasma discharge -> purge
Purge -> reactant pulse -> precursor pulse -> ramp-up
items.explanation: The essence of ALD is separating two half-reactions in time. The precursor pulse saturates surface reaction sites, a purge removes unreacted precursor and byproducts, the reactant pulse exchanges surface ligands, and another purge follows. A purge must sit between the two pulses to preserve self-limiting behavior; without it, the two pulses would meet in the gas phase and react like CVD, breaking self-limitation.

items.stem: When depositing a dielectric inside a trench of aspect ratio 10:1, which option correctly pairs the definition of step coverage with the conformality ranking (thickness uniformity over the whole structure) of sputter PVD, CVD, and ALD?
choices: Step coverage = top thickness / sidewall thickness, and conformality ranks sputter PVD > CVD > ALD
Step coverage = sidewall (or bottom) thickness / top thickness, and conformality ranks ALD > CVD > sputter PVD
Step coverage = trench depth / trench width, and conformality ranks CVD > ALD > sputter PVD
Step coverage = bottom thickness / trench width, and all three are identical regardless of aspect ratio
items.explanation: Step coverage measures how well the film follows onto the trench sidewall and bottom relative to the flat (top) field, so SC = sidewall (or bottom) thickness divided by top thickness, and the closer to 1 (100 %) the better. The point is that top thickness is the denominator; putting it in the numerator inverts the definition. Trench depth divided by width is not step coverage at all, it is the definition of aspect ratio. The ranking follows from how material reaches and reacts at the surface. In sputter PVD the arriving flux is close to line-of-sight, so material lands only where it can be seen from the source, an overhang builds at the entrance and deeper regions fall into shadow. CVD reaches further in by gas-phase diffusion and so beats sputtering, but as long as growth tracks the local arrival rate the entrance stays thicker. ALD is self-limiting at the surface: once one exposure saturates the surface no more is added, so with sufficient exposure the deep regions saturate to the same thickness as the entrance. Hence conformality ranks ALD > CVD > sputter PVD. The claim that all three are identical regardless of aspect ratio contradicts this entire picture.

items.stem: In a medium-current ion implanter, what is the correct order of the ion path from the ion source to the wafer?
choices: Ion source -> acceleration column -> mass-analyzing magnet -> resolving aperture -> scanner -> end station
Ion source -> extraction electrode -> mass-analyzing magnet -> resolving aperture -> acceleration column -> scanner -> end station
Ion source -> scanner -> extraction electrode -> acceleration column -> mass-analyzing magnet -> end station
Extraction electrode -> ion source -> resolving aperture -> mass-analyzing magnet -> acceleration column -> end station
items.explanation: Ions are generated at the ion source, extracted by the extraction electrode into a beam, split by trajectory according to mass-to-charge ratio at the mass-analyzing magnet, filtered to only the target species at the resolving aperture, accelerated or decelerated to the target energy in the acceleration column, scanned across the wafer by the scanner, and finally reach the wafer at the end station. Mass analysis must happen right after extraction (bending a beam after it is accelerated would need an unrealistically large magnet), and the resolving aperture must sit right after the magnet since its job is to filter the trajectories the magnet just separated.

items.stem: In an ion implanter, name the component that applies a magnetic field to a beam of mixed ion species extracted from the ion source, bending each species along a different radius of curvature by mass-to-charge ratio (m/q) so that only the target species passes the downstream resolving aperture.
items.explanation: The beam extracted from the ion source contains not only the target dopant ion but also molecular ions, multiply charged ions, and impurity ions mixed together. Since these differ in mass-to-charge ratio, a uniform magnetic field bends each along a different radius, and the part that uses this to bend only the target m/q along the correct curvature into the resolving aperture is the mass-analyzing magnet. The resolving aperture is only a hole that filters one of the trajectories the magnet already separated and cannot bend ions itself, so it cannot be the answer to a question asking which part does the bending.

items.stem: Within the ALD window and with saturated precursor exposure, all other conditions are unchanged and only the cycle count is doubled. Which outcome is correct?
choices: Film thickness doubles and GPC is halved
Film thickness doubles and GPC is unchanged
Film thickness scales by sqrt(2) and GPC is unchanged
Film thickness is unchanged and only film density doubles
items.explanation: Under saturated ALD, GPC (growth per cycle) is a constant independent of cycle count, because every cycle repeats the same self-limiting reaction. This gives film thickness = cycle count * GPC, a strict proportionality, so doubling cycle count exactly doubles thickness. A sqrt-scaling slowdown is instead the signature of diffusion-limited growth and does not apply to ALD, whose reaction terminates at the surface.

items.stem: A saturated ALD process runs at GPC = 1.20 angstrom/cycle. One cycle consists of 0.20 s precursor pulse + 2.00 s purge + 0.30 s reactant pulse + 2.50 s purge. How many seconds of net deposition time are needed to obtain a 24.0 nm thick film? (Ignore overhead such as ramp-up and loading. 1 nm = 10 angstrom.)
items.explanation: Target thickness 24.0 nm = 240 angstrom. Required cycles N = 240/1.20 = 200 cycles. Cycle time = 0.20+2.00+0.30+2.50 = 5.00 s. Net deposition time = 200*5.00 = 1000 s. Answering just the cycle count 200, or the minutes value 16.7 without converting, is wrong, and misapplying GPC to get 240 cycles gives the wrong answer 1200.

items.stem: Target dose and implant energy are held fixed, and only beam current is raised from 1.0 mA to 4.0 mA. Which statement is correct? (Scan area and ion charge state unchanged.)
choices: The implant time to reach the target dose shrinks to about 1/4, improving throughput, but the charge arriving per unit time at the wafer quadruples, increasing the risk of surface charging and wafer heating
Implant time quadruples and the final dose also quadruples
The ions strike 4 times harder, so projected range R_p becomes about 4 times deeper
Since dose is proportional to beam current, implant time must also be quadrupled to hit the target dose
items.explanation: From the dose equation Q = I*t/(q*A), with Q and A fixed, t is proportional to 1/I, so quadrupling beam current cuts implant time to 1/4 and improves throughput. But since the charge delivered per unit time quadruples, the risk of surface charging and wafer heating rises. Projected range R_p is set by energy (accelerating voltage), not beam current, so depth is unaffected, and since a Faraday cup integrates charge to end the implant at the target dose, deliberately also extending the time would instead multiply the dose by 16.

items.stem: Singly charged boron ions (11B+) are implanted into silicon. Beam current I = 2.0 mA, scan area A = 400 cm^2, implant time t = 40 s, and the straggle at this energy is delta-R_p = 40 nm. If the implant profile follows the Gaussian N(x) = N_p*exp(-(x-R_p)^2/2*delta-R_p^2), find the peak concentration N_p. (q = 1.602e-19 C, sqrt(2*pi) = 2.5066, 1 nm = 1e-7 cm)
items.explanation: Dose Q = I*t/(q*A) = (2.0e-3*40)/(1.602e-19*400) = 0.080/(6.408e-17) ~= 1.248e15 ions/cm^2. delta-R_p = 40 nm = 4.0e-6 cm. Since the area under the Gaussian equals the dose, N_p = Q/(sqrt(2*pi)*delta-R_p) = 1.248e15/(2.5066*4.0e-6) ~= 1.25e20 cm⁻³. Stopping at the dose gives the dimensionally wrong 1.25e15 cm^-2, and omitting sqrt(2*pi) to compute Q/delta-R_p only overestimates by about 2.5x, giving 3.12e20.

items.stem: In an ion-implantation process, boron is implanted with the wafer untilted (tilt 0, twist 0), and at the same energy and dose, a long shallow tail appears behind the profile peak (R_p) and junction depth ends up about 60% deeper than target. Name this phenomenon.
items.explanation: Because silicon is a single crystal, along certain crystallographic directions atoms line up to form open channels where an ion collides with almost nothing. With the wafer normal to the beam, many ions enter these channels and travel deep without nuclear collisions, leaving a long shallow tail behind the peak and a deeper-than-predicted junction. Countermeasures include a 7-degree tilt, a twist angle, a screen oxide, and pre-amorphization implants. Thermal diffusion during anneal instead broadens both shoulders of the profile and lowers the peak height, which is a different signature from the tail appearing only behind the peak described here.

items.stem: A trench 50 nm wide and 750 nm deep (aspect ratio 15) is coated with an ALD dielectric, implanted with boron, and annealed for activation. Three things are observed at once: (a) top film thickness 20.0 nm, bottom film thickness 8.0 nm (40% step coverage); (b) overhang at the trench opening with a sealed void below it; (c) sheet resistance about 2.5x the target (450 ohm/sq). Substrate temperature was 250 degC (within the ALD window), and junction depth and doping-profile peak position were normal. Which cause-and-fix combination is most plausible?
choices: The precursor pulse and purge fell short of the saturation exposure needed at aspect ratio 15, starving deep-trench exposure; separately, the activation anneal's thermal budget was insufficient -> lengthen the precursor pulse and purge to secure saturation, and raise anneal temperature to spec
Substrate temperature dropped below the ALD window and the precursor condensed -> raise substrate temperature into the decomposition region above the window
Low implant energy giving a shallow R_p is the root cause -> double the implant energy
Insufficient ALD cycle count is the cause -> simply double the cycle count
items.explanation: A 40% step coverage together with overhang and a void is a classic signature of insufficient exposure. As aspect ratio grows, the exposure (pulse time times pressure) needed to saturate deep locations rises sharply, so when exposure falls short the opening saturates first, forming an overhang that seals a void beneath it. Meanwhile, normal junction depth and profile peak but 2.5x sheet resistance means the dopant landed in the right place but was not electrically activated, pointing to an insufficient thermal budget in the activation anneal. This is an independent overlap of a deposition-side cause and an anneal-side cause; simply doubling cycle count would scale top and bottom thickness by the same factor without changing the ratio that defines step coverage, and it would not explain the sheet-resistance anomaly at all. One clarification. The roughly 2.5x ratio of sheet resistance to target is a condition posed by this item, not a value reported in any particular reference. What the literature supports is the direction only, that insufficient activation raises sheet resistance; the actual multiple depends on process, material, and measurement conditions.
